correctness.rationale: The frozen formulas are mathematically correct; the substantive repair narrows the claim, not the estimates. Affine independence follows from ker L=span(1); w_x=L^dagger e_x satisfies w_x·Le_y=delta_xy-1/N, so -w_x is outward and the interior angle has cosine -c_h/a. Each difference of weight h gives N/2 pairs. The inverse-square multiplier 1/(4|S|^2) yields a convergent integral of t times the product heat kernel minus its stationary term; at every t>0 the product strictly decreases with h, hence so do the interior angles. Comparing the linear coefficient at u=0 of the binomial expansion and finite product for the beta integral B(u,d+1) gives c_d=-(H_d^2+H_d^(2))/(8N). The adjacent entry is positive for d>=3 by the first term of the one-coordinate difference sum and is -1/64 at d=2. Parseval gives the shell sum including h=0; remove a^2 and divide by a^2 to obtain the normalized off-diagonal energy. For X=(2K-d)/d with K fair binomial, the cubic Taylor expansions of (1+X)^(-2), (1+X)^(-4) and -X(1+X)^(-2) on |X|<=1/2 use E X^2=1/d and E X^4=(3d^2-2d)/d^4, with odd moments zero. The tails are exponentially small even after the inverse-power bounds. This gives a=d^(-2)(1+3/d+O(d^-2)), b=d^(-4)(1+10/d+O(d^-2)) and c_1=d^(-2)(2/d+O(d^-2)). Both all nonzero differences and the Hamming-one contribution have leading energy 4/d in shell normalization, with O(d^-2) errors, establishing the asserted share and mean. The exact antipodal value then gives the other asymptotic by expansion of arccos. A newly written rational replay solved two radial Poisson equations using shell-neighbor counts, matching all Walsh shells, energy, monotonicity, signs and antipodal values for d=2..30; the estimates remain analytical.
residual_risks: The metric is inherited from the full columns of L, not the simplex of Gram L or an arbitrary affine image. The replay is finite and does not certify the asymptotics.

value.rationale: The repaired result identifies which ridges account for nearly all deviation energy even though the fraction of such ridges tends to zero exponentially. A typical ridge therefore hides a strong local signal; the mean and the two disparate extreme scales quantify this distinction. These conclusions give a usable metric description beyond computing an already known pointwise kernel or tabulating finite dimensions.
residual_risks: The interpretation applies to equal-weight squared cosines in the full Euclidean column realization, not a weighted curvature measure or a general Laplacian-simplex law.
